[E2, E13]

Plume is large diffuse aged/detached haze: area 38772 km2 length 355 km, centroid 374.7 km from Kilauea, wind-based upwind end 359.7 km from Kilauea, tracked source end 285.8 km N-NW of Kilauea at 21.75N 156.41W. [E4, E11, E8]

Motion disagreement must lower confidence: tracked drift toward 300 deg WNW vs wind toward ~19 deg NNE differs by ~79 deg despite good fit R2 0.76 at 5.6 kmh; mask swallows Oahu at 98.1% with land_frac 0.041, so island portion of mask is unreliable. [E8, E2, E6]

evidence: Same paused Kilauea and quiet Mauna Loa status; no FIRMS fire clusters in region, so wildfire_smoke not supported but volcanic link also not proven for this veil. [E1, E10]

Geometry far from vents and not vent-attached: centroid 407.0 km from Kilauea, wind-based upwind end 507.6 km SW over open ocean at 20.005N 160.09W, tracked source end 343.9 km from Kilauea. [E5, E12, E9]

Wind at veil 24.9 kmh from 229 deg blows toward ~49 deg NE; this would carry Big Island emissions NE, not to a veil centered west of the island chain at 20.506N 158.997W, so location is not clearly downwind of either summit. [E3]

Measured drift toward 261 deg W disagrees with wind toward ~49 deg by ~148 deg (near opposite), but fit R2 0.01 and speed 1.6 kmh mean motion is noise and cannot confirm or refute transport; disagreement stated and lowers confidence. [E9, E3]

Mask entirely oceanic (land_frac 0.0) very faint gray veil thinner and grayer than surrounding white clouds, but without transport/source link cannot distinguish aged vog from thin cirrus/haze artifact. [E7]

classify.caveats: Kilauea was paused (not erupting) at image time, so vog would be from passive degassing/residual rather than active eruption. Plume 1 tracked drift (toward 300 deg) disagrees with wind (toward ~19 deg) by ~79 deg despite good fit, lowering confidence. Plume 1 mask swallows Oahu (98% coverage) so part of mask is unreliable. Plume 2 motion fit is noise (R2 0.01) and geometry is far from vents. No SO2 or aerosol composition measurement; no fire attribution beyond FIRMS box search.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Precursory overflows started yesterday afternoon, but stopped overnight during summit deflation. A forecast window of September 8-10 is likely for the start of episode 55.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
